Dear [[PERSON|w1,w9|Tomasz]],

Thank you for the photographs. I have now read the tenancy agreement for [[ADDRESS||Flat 3, 18 Marsh Lane, Leeds LS9 8AB]]. Your landlord, [[ORG||Harrowgate Lettings Ltd]] (company no. [[ID|w8|11829304]]), failed to protect your deposit within 30 days, which is a breach of [[NOT||section 213 of the Housing Act 2004]]. The [[NOT||Deposit Protection Service]] has no record of it. That gives you a claim for between one and three times the deposit.

The letting agent's manager, [[PERSON|w5|Gary Young]], told me on the phone that "young Mr [[PERSON|w2,w3,w9|Wróbel]]" had agreed to an unprotected deposit. That is not a defence. I will send a letter before claim under the [[NOT||Pre-Action Conduct Practice Direction]] this week and, if needed, issue in the [[NOT||County Court at Leeds]].

My colleague [[PERSON|w5|Daniel Price]] will handle the costs side; please note that the [[NOT||price]] we quoted is fixed.

PARTICULARS OF CLAIM

1. The Claimant, [[PERSON|w5|Anthony Mason]], is a retired teacher who lives at [[ADDRESS||44 Lordship Lane, London SE22 8HJ]] (the "Property").

2. The Defendant is a company registered in England and Wales (company number [[ID|w8|08812376]]) which designs and fits kitchens. Its sole director is [[PERSON|w4,w9|Dmitri Volkov]].

3. By a written contract dated 2 February 2026 the Defendant agreed to supply and install a kitchen at the Property for £24,600. Mr [[PERSON|w3,w5|Mason]] paid a deposit of £12,300 on the same day.

4. It was an implied term, under [[NOT||section 49 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015]], that the work would be carried out with reasonable care and skill.

5. In breach of that term the Defendant's fitter, a [[NOT||mason]] by trade named [[PERSON|w1,w5|Kit Carver]], cut the worktops incorrectly and left the gas hob unsecured. The Claimant's neighbour, [[PERSON|w5|Rosemary Hunter]], witnessed the hob detach on 9 April 2026.

6. The Claimant complained by e-mail from [[EMAIL|w1,w8|tony.mason44@btinternet.com]] on 10 April 2026. [[PERSON|w2,w3,w9|Volkov's]] reply of 14 April 2026 denied liability.

7. As a result, the Claimant has suffered loss and damage. Following the incident he suffered [[OTHER||a minor burn to his left hand and anxiety, for which he was treated at King's College Hospital]].

PARTICULARS OF LOSS
(a) Cost of remedial works (quotation of [[ORG|w5|Mason & Hunter Joinery]], no connection with the Claimant or the witness): £15,900
(b) General damages for pain, suffering and loss of amenity: £2,500
(c) Loss of use of kitchen, 16 weeks at £60: £960

8. The Claimant claims interest under [[NOT||section 69 of the County Courts Act 1984]] at 8% per year.

9. The Claimant reported the unsecured hob to [[NOT||Gas Safe Register]] and to [[NOT||Southwark Council]] Trading Standards. The Defendant's filings at [[NOT||Companies House]] show it as active. The claim is suitable for the fast track under [[NOT||Part 26 of the Civil Procedure Rules]].

AND THE CLAIMANT CLAIMS: damages limited to £25,000, interest and costs.

STATEMENT OF TRUTH
I believe that the facts stated in these Particulars of Claim are true. I understand that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes a false statement without an honest belief in its truth.
